_about: Battle tuning for BattleSim.gd. Troop values come from prototype/battle_core.js; generals are new (start: ~6x a soldier, tune with tools/run_sims.gd). Times are seconds, distances are field pixels (480x240).

units._generals_note: Generals, starting point from run_sims: slime general 6x hp / 3x atk of a big slime; knight general 5x hp / ~2.6x atk of a knight (6x/3x made slimes win only 5-20%). A bit slower than troops. engage_range = fights enemies this close; follow_gap = hangs this far behind its troops.

_orders_note: advance = AI default from the prototype: walks in, no bonuses.
_formations_note: Spots are for an army facing right (left side of the field); a side facing left mirrors x as width - x. flank = extra atk when flank_min or more allies hit the same target. Roles toward generals: general_pull (<1 = enemy general counts as closer when picking targets, applied to squared distance), envelop (px troops swing above/below the enemy general), leash (px troops stay within of their own general).

_specials_note: All specials sweep from the caster's edge (start_x) to end_x at speed, a band width px deep, hitting each enemy once. lane_height 0 = full field height; > 0 = a lane that tall, aimed by the caster (AI or best lane for the player). knockback = px survivors are pushed back. type/color are for BattleView.

specials._cavalry_note: Knight general. run_sims 300/combo vs enemy AI (slime player, special on): line charge 46%, square charge 65%. mp_cost 85 = about one charge per battle; damage 10 / mp 70 dropped slime line-charge to 24%.

cavalry_charge.label: ทัพม้าบุกทะลวง

_ai_note: BattleAI (enemy side), see scripts/battle/BattleAI.gd. Every think_interval s: hit value per enemy = share of max HP taken + kill_bonus if it dies, general x general_weight. Cast when the best lane holds min_share of the value of hitting every enemy; full MP lowers it to full_mp_min_share; own general below danger_hp with enemies within danger_range: any hit, those enemies x danger_weight.
_sides_note: Side order matters: units spawn interleaved in this order, and if both armies die on the same step the first side wins (prototype behaviour).
